First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}-2X-8 \\  & ={X}^{2}-2X-8I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(A)={A}^{2}-2A-8I.$

Let's calculate ${A}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{2} & =A\cdot A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 10 \\ 15 & 22\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(A):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(A) & ={A}^{2}-2A-8I \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 10 \\ 15 & 22\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}]-8[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 10 \\ 15 & 22\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 & -4 \\ -6 & -8\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 \\ 0 & -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7-2-8 & 10-4+0 \\ 15-6+0 & 22-8-8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 \\ 9 & 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
